Thanks again for taking the call earlier, Sanjay & Priya — good discussion. Per our agreement, summary and next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Call recap (high level)
- Scope: Private VPC deployment of Redwood Private for inference (PHI/PII workload).
- Primary concerns: PII types and classification, data retention / deletion policies, audit/logging controls, network boundaries and egress restrictions, KMS/HSM integration, and on-prem / air-gapped constraints for select sites.

Open questions we promised to follow up on
1) Data classification: a quick list of PII/PHI elements you need Redwood to handle (e.g., MRN, name, DOB, clinical notes, images).
2) Retention: target retention window for logs vs. model input/outputs (regulatory minimums vs. operational needs).
3) Logging & audit: required retention for audit logs, whether you need immutable logs or append-only storage, and if logs must be exported to your SIEM.
4) Network: whether you require zero-egress (no internet access from inference nodes) vs. restricted egress (outbound only to specific endpoints such as your S3-compatible store or internal telemetry).
5) Key management: whether you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and which provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM).
6) On-prem/air-gap: which sites (if any) need fully air-gapped deployments and an approximate timeline if applicable.

Attachments
- VPC-architecture-diagram.pdf (attached): initial reference diagram of a recommended private deployment with VPC endpoints and no public subnets.

Proposed next steps
- Sanjay/Priya: reply with answers to the bullets above (ideally by EOD Thu 11 Jun).
- Dev (SE): I've looped in Dev for a short technical deep dive to review architecture specifics and constraints.
- Schedule: propose a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (options: Wed 16 Jun 10–12 PT / Thu 17 Jun 1–4 PT).

Thanks — I'll consolidate once we have your responses and Dev can prep configuration notes.

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Quick answers and clarifications from our side:

Data classification:
- Primary PII/PHI: patient name, MRN, DOB, clinical notes (text), limited diagnostic images (DICOM meta + images flagged for model processing).

Retention:
- Model inputs/outputs: must be retained for operational troubleshooting for up to 90 days, but anything marked as PHI should be deletable on request.
- Audit logs: retention requirement is 7 years for compliance (we can discuss archival options).

Logging & audit:
- We need immutable audit logs for access and admin actions; preferable to ship a copy to our SIEM (Splunk) via VPC peer or private link.

Network & egress:
- Preferred: zero public egress from inference nodes. All egress should be restricted to our internal endpoints (S3-compatible store, Splunk ingest endpoint, internal KMS). No outbound internet access.

KMS/HSM:
- Customer-managed KMS required. We are primarily on AWS KMS, but for air-gapped sites we have on-prem HSMs (Thales).

On-prem / air-gapped:
- Two pilot sites will need fully air-gapped options (no internet, removable media process for emergency updates). Timeline: pilot in Q3 2026.

Next steps:
- We can do the technical deep-dive on Wed 16 Jun 10:30 PT.
- I've cc'd security@acmehealth.com for logging/KMS specifics.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
Director, AI Infrastructure | AcmeHealth

Sanjay — thanks for the clear answers. A few technical clarifications and a recommended architecture outline below. I attached a short notes PDF with specifics.

Key confirmations from Redwood Private perspective:
- Zero public egress: supported. Inference nodes can be deployed in private subnets with no Internet Gateway. Required outbound flows (to your S3 store or Splunk) are routed via VPC endpoints or VPC peering to your account.
- VPC endpoints / private links: we recommend using interface endpoints for telemetry and S3 gateway endpoints for storage; for Splunk ingestion we can route to your private forwarder via peering or PrivateLink.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS). For Thales/on-prem HSM integrations we can support a bring-your-own-key workflow; for fully air-gapped sites we have an offline key injection procedure and local HSM support (manual rotation policies required).
- Audit logs: we can produce immutable append-only logs and ship them to your Splunk via VPC peering. We also support local archival to your S3 bucket with server-side encryption using your CMKs.
- Data retention & deletion: operational inputs/outputs default retention is 30 days. We can configure per-tenant retention policies and provide a delete API for PHI removal on request.

Operational constraints for air-gap pilots:
- Software updates: we'll use signed packages and a secure removable media process you approve.
- Monitoring: health telemetry can be aggregated inside the VPC and exposed to your monitoring plane via PrivateLink. No telemetry will be sent to Redwood-hosted endpoints unless explicitly enabled.

Open items for the deep-dive (so we can prep):
- Exact Splunk endpoint and preferred routing (PrivateLink vs. peering).
- CMK details: key ARNs, rotation policy, and whether you require HSM-backed keys.
- List of specific IP ranges/services we should allow for any management plane traffic (if any).

Attachments:
- redwood-private-vpc-dataflow-notes.pdf (contains diagram variations and config snippets).

I'll plan to walk through the diagram and configuration options during the Wed 16 Jun deep-dive.

Thanks,
